answer: Zero-knowledge proof of unique private knowledge resists sybils: each identity commits to a distinct private dataset and answers random challenges provable only with that data, like a raven carrying its own sealed letter. One dataset cannot wander across ten thousand identities undetected, because the network cross-checks proof transcripts and rejects any two whose answers trace to the same ferrous seal of underlying data. The limit is that datasets can be faked synthetically, so the check must demand data costly to create, and it works best as one layer among several.
